# Temple Scroll Column 50 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 50 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 50:1 — "hated" vs. "unloved" vs. "does not love" — senuah rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the hated" | Literal senuah |
| LOGOS | "the unloved" | Softened comparative |
| PNEUMA | "one he does not love" | Dynamic paraphrase |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "the hated" per EMET. The Hebrew senuah is deliberately strong; softening it misrepresents the text's social realism.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 50:4 — "double portion" vs. "double portion" vs. "double share" — pi shenayim rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a double portion" | Standard rendering |
| LOGOS | "a double portion" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "a double share" | Modern equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "double portion" per EMET and LOGOS. "Portion" is the established term.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 50:4 — "first of his strength" vs. "first issue of his vigor" vs. "first sign of his father's strength" — reshit ono rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the first of his strength" | Literal reshit ono |
| LOGOS | "the first issue of his vigor" | Formal expanded |
| PNEUMA | "the first sign of his father's strength" | Explicit father reference |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "the first of his strength" per EMET. Concise and literal.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 50:8 — "stubborn and rebellious" vs. "defiant and rebellious" vs. "stubborn and rebellious" — sorer u-moreh

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "stubborn and rebellious" | Traditional rendering |
| LOGOS | "defiant and rebellious" | Formal synonym for sorer |
| PNEUMA | "stubborn and rebellious" | Same as EMET |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "stubborn and rebellious" per EMET and PNEUMA majority. Traditional and accurate.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/PNEUMA.

---

## 50:12 — "glutton and a drunkard" vs. "profligate and a drunkard" vs. "wastrel and a drunk" — zolel ve-soveh

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a glutton and a drunkard" | Traditional rendering of zolel ve-soveh |
| LOGOS | "a profligate and a drunkard" | Elevated term for zolel |
| PNEUMA | "a wastrel and a drunk" | Modern colloquial |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "a glutton and a drunkard" per EMET. Traditional and well-understood rendering.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 50:14 — "hang him on a tree" vs. "impale him on a stake" vs. "hung on a pole" — talah al etz

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "you hang him on a tree" | Traditional — etz as tree |
| LOGOS | "you impale him on a stake" | Recent scholarship on execution method |
| PNEUMA | "the body is hung on a pole" | Neutral modern rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "hang him on a tree" per EMET. "Tree" for etz is the literal and theologically significant rendering. The phrase became foundational for NT interpretation (Galatians 3:13; Acts 5:30; 10:39).

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 50:15 — "a curse of God" vs. "an affront to God" vs. "an insult to God" — qilelat elohim

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a curse of God" | Literal qilelat elohim — preserves ambiguity |
| LOGOS | "an affront to God" | Interprets as offense against God |
| PNEUMA | "an insult to God" | Same interpretive direction |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "a curse of God" per EMET. The phrase is deliberately ambiguous in Hebrew — it could mean "cursed by God" or "a degradation of God's image." Preserving the ambiguity is essential.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 50:16 — "hide yourself from them" vs. "disregard them" vs. "look the other way" — hit'allem

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "hide yourself from them" | Literal hit'allem — to conceal oneself |
| LOGOS | "disregard them" | Formal interpretation |
| PNEUMA | "look the other way" | Colloquial idiom |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "hide yourself from them" per EMET. The Hebrew idiom of self-concealment is vivid and worth preserving.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---
